documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 01/19/2021

Three months after stopping procainamide. The facial rash and the evening fevers have resolved. Myalgias gone. Joints back to his usual rheumatoid pattern: brief morning stiffness in the hands, no new swelling.
Current medications: amiodarone 200 mg daily (cardiology), methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: no rash. No synovitis today. Heart and lungs normal.
ESR 12, normal.

Assessment: procainamide-induced lupus, resolved off the drug. Seropositive RA, low activity.
Plan: continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid and prednisone 5 mg. Avoid procainamide in future. Monitoring labs every 3 months, fine to draw through his PCP. Return in 6 months.

conditions.label: History of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Rash gone, no fevers since November. Rheum saw him in January, calls the lupus resolved. Amiodarone 200 daily without trouble, no cough or breathlessness, no visual change, no tremor.
Home BP 120s/70s.
Exam: skin clear, heart regular, lungs clear, joints quiet.
A/P: Procainamide-induced lupus, resolved; listed as history. He knows not to take procainamide again. RA stable, labs today. Amiodarone, TSH/LFTs due May. COVID vaccine: eligible now with his immunosuppression, encouraged him to book at the pharmacy. RTC June.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check. Feels fine, working long days with the summer build schedule. Wearing a hat and long sleeves on site since the lupus scare. Sneezy in May, manages it himself.
Meds unchanged. Pulse in the 60s on amiodarone, no lightheadedness.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Hands without synovitis.
A/P: HTN at goal. RA quiet. Amiodarone labs from May normal. Allergic rhinitis, seasonal, nothing prescribed. Flu and COVID booster in the fall. Physical February.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu quadrivalent IM left deltoid. Moderna booster (third dose, immunocompromised) IM right deltoid. VIS and EUA fact sheet given. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thyroid, liver and blood counts unremarkable. Message to pt.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. No complaints. Winter is his slow season. Joints fine, rheum last saw him in the fall. Amiodarone, no breathing or vision issues. Cardiology yearly visit in the fall, no letter came through this time.
ROS negative. PHQ-2 0.
Exam: BMI ~28. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin, no rash. Joints: no active synovitis. Neuro nonfocal.
A/P
- HTN, at goal.
- Seropositive RA, stable regimen.
- Hx VT on amiodarone; TSH/LFTs every 6 months, last ones normal.
- Immunosuppressed: PCV20 today and first Shingrix today, agreed this year. Second Shingrix in 2 to 6 months.
- Lipids, CMP, CBC today. Colonoscopy due 2024.

events.reason: right knee injury after fall from ladder

reports.text: Right knee, three views. No acute fracture or dislocation. The patella sits abnormally low relative to the femoral condyles. Soft tissue swelling anterior to the knee.
reports.conclusion: No fracture. Abnormal, low-lying patella, in keeping with the clinical concern for extensor mechanism disruption.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED
Visit: 04/12/2022

CC: right knee injury.
HPI: 58 year old man with seropositive RA and prior procainamide-associated lupus. Lost his footing coming down a ladder, landed with the right knee bent, felt and heard a pop. Immediate severe pain, swelling, could not get up or bear weight.
PMH: hypertension, rheumatoid arthritis, history of ventricular tachycardia, seasonal allergies, drug-induced lupus, H. pylori 2019.
Meds: methotrexate 15 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid, amiodarone 200 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol, construction site supervisor.

Exam: right knee swollen with bruising. Palpable defect just above the patella; patella rides lower than the left. Cannot extend the knee against gravity. Distal pulses and sensation intact. Other extremities normal.
Imaging: right knee X-ray, no fracture, abnormal patellar position.

Assessment: right quadriceps tendon rupture.
Plan: knee immobilizer in extension, crutches, non-weight-bearing. Orthopedics consulted; surgical repair scheduled 04/14. Avoid NSAIDs. Follow up with PCP after surgery.

events.reason: repair of right quadriceps tendon rupture

documents.title: Operative Report: right quadriceps tendon repair
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 04/14/2022
Preoperative diagnosis: right quadriceps tendon rupture.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: primary repair of right quadriceps tendon.
Anesthesia: general with adductor canal block.

Findings: complete rupture of the quadriceps tendon at its insertion on the superior pole of the patella. Patellar cartilage and patellar tendon intact.
Description: midline incision. Hematoma evacuated. Tendon edges debrided. Three longitudinal transosseous tunnels drilled through the patella; tendon repaired with heavy nonabsorbable sutures in a running locking pattern, tied over the inferior pole bridge. Repair tested to 30 degrees of flexion without gapping. Layered closure.
EBL minimal. No complications.

Disposition: overnight observation, discharged 04/15. Hinged knee brace locked in extension, weight bearing as tolerated in the brace. Follow-up in 2 weeks for wound check; PT to begin after that visit with gradual unlocking of the brace.

documents.title: Post-op check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after ED notice and knee surgery 4/14. Home, brace locked straight, getting around on crutches. Pain controlled. Incision dry per his look under the dressing. No calf pain or swelling, no fever. Asked whether to keep methotrexate and prednisone going, ortho told him yes. Booked PCP follow-up 4/28. Reminded: no ibuprofen or naproxen.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-op Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from right quadriceps tendon repair. Saw ortho Tuesday for wound check, staples out, starting PT next week. Brace on, locked in extension, walking with one crutch. Pain 2-3/10.
On prednisone and MTX, discussed that steroids can slow tendon healing; ortho aware. Not on anticoagulation.
Exam: brace in place, incision clean and healed, mild swelling. Calves soft, nontender, no asymmetry. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P: Right quad tendon rupture s/p repair. PT per ortho. Off work for now, paperwork completed for his employer. Watch for calf swelling or chest symptoms. We have the ED record but no operative report; requested. Second Shingrix when he's past the early recovery, June or so.

documents.title: Operative note filed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Operative report for 4/14 right quadriceps repair received from the hospital after our request and scanned to Procedures.

documents.title: Orthopedic Follow-up
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopedic surgery clinic
Visit: 06/21/2022

Nine weeks after right quadriceps tendon repair. Doing well. Brace now unlocked to 60 degrees and progressing per protocol with physical therapy twice weekly. Incision healed. Quadriceps contraction good, extensor mechanism intact, can perform a straight-leg raise. Flexion to 75 degrees.
Plan: continue PT, wean brace over the next month, return to light duty at about 3 months and full duty around 5 to 6 months as strength allows. Follow up in 6 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four months post quad repair. Out of the brace, still in PT once a week, back at work on light duty since mid-July, mostly in the site trailer. Stairs getting easier. No pain at rest.
BP fine. RA ok. Amiodarone, due TSH/LFTs.
Exam: right knee incision well healed, flexion near full, mild quad atrophy compared to left, extension strong against resistance. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
A/P: Quad tendon repair recovering on schedule. TSH, LFTs, CBC, BMP today. Second Shingrix today (series complete). Flu/bivalent COVID booster in October.
